restrictions: Target sha256-r37-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..36 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is verified with the target before it is returned.

Algorithm: the two-block attack of Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian and Zhu (IACR ePrint 2026/1120) with its 37-step characteristic and the Step-1 solution S of its published SFS pair, as transcribed in filing 6c77089c. A0 carries no condition, so S has 12,103,680 variants (proof.md 4.3); the attack uses the 782,800 variants of the 222 c7-classes of at least 3456 variants. Per first block: one bit-sliced W7 test of all classes (exact set F7), bit-sliced W6 programs (exact set F6) for each passing class, good pairs in groups of four 64-bit lanes (u = W0 + s0(W1)), a row-16 presence word, the exact row-16 table over the 32 elements of L*, rows 17..36 with early abort.

Cost: fixed caps N_FB = 357,577,563,488,735,156 first blocks (2^58.31103; one target compression plus 421 counted operations each) and V_MAX = 15,844,143,000,526,062,945,838 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded), with A_C = 2^60, A_S = 2^50, DEV = 2^40 and 2^40 operations of precomputation: 2^62.713293 target compressions on every run (proof.md Section 11), claimed 62.7133. Every target compression is charged one unit; the W7 and W6 filters are bit-sliced and good pairs are processed four per word (scalar W6: 64.91364; scalar u: 63.11917).

Success probability at least 0.3900000047 under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks), H2 (q3 >= 2^-74.0252, the one-sided 99% lower bound of a preregistered 32-replicate Monte-Carlo estimate over the 222 classes) and H3 (at most 2^-9.4 further successes expected in the same first block); Chebyshev bounds the work-cap overflow below 2^-21.4. No expected-work bound and no independence-of-conditions model is used.

Memory is a reported metric only (2^34.2 bytes: the F6/F7 bitmaps, the 2^32-entry row-16 table and its presence table, the lane-scan table, the class data). baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings (two uniform 256-bit words each); their chaining values CV1 = F_37(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: for every fixed variant a0, Pr[W7x in F7] = p7 = |F7|/2^32 and Pr[W6x in F6 | W7x in F7] = p6 = |F6|/2^32 exactly, and given both, W0..W5 are uniform and independent of (W6, W7), which are uniform on F6 x F7 (proof.md Lemma 5.1); hence g = 782,800 x p7 x p6 = 830.988 good pairs per first block in expectation; distinct first blocks are independent (success bound and the Chebyshev bound on the work cap).
heuristics.scope: The expected numbers of passing classes, good pairs and row-16 passes per first block; the law of the second-block words that defines q3; independence across first blocks (proof.md Section 10). Not the validity of any output: every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured with the attack's own filters on real first blocks (proof.md Section 13.1): 2^17.58 and 2^23 first blocks (random M0, real 37-step compressions, all 222 classes): passing classes 696,209 and 29,623,852 against 692,640 and 29,552,640 expected; good pairs 163,607,020 and 6,997,476,590 against 163,378,921.9 and 6,970,834,000 (ratios 1.0014 and 1.0038); row-16 passes 40,079 and 1,712,536 against 40,099.1 and 1,715,041.6 (z = -0.10, -1.91). The counts are bursty because class tests are correlated (variance 28.8 x mean for the number of passing classes on 2 x 10^7 uniform words, so the passing-class excess of 0.24% at 2^23 is +2.4 standard deviations and the good-pair excess +2.1; both lower the cost); the means are exact under H1. The 64-class runs of 087a18c4 (2^21 and 2^23 first blocks) agree within 0.6%. The organizer experiment a0-online-r37 runs the counted online program on organizer-seeded first blocks. These are 2^23 trials, not 2^58.
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem; tested on 2^23 first blocks. The class tests of one first block are strongly correlated (their c7 values are close), so per-first-block counts are overdispersed; only their expectations and the independence across first blocks are used.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 782,800 selected variants and the 32 elements of L* of Pr[rows 16..36 of both members follow every cell and every printed two-bit condition closing at rows >= 16 (corrected reading A15[29] = A17[29])] satisfies 2^-74.0252 = q3_model <= q3 <= 2^-70 (H6 fixes q3_model at the printed one-sided 99% lower bound of the second study, rounded down at the fourth decimal of its logarithm).
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g 32 q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Lemma 7.1 (proof.md): rows 16..22 have exactly the same probability for every variant (W8 does not occur in W16..W22 and their law is the same for every variant by Lemma 5.1); a variant enters rows >= 23 only through W8 in W23 and W24, with fixed modular differences, so only the four W24 conditions can depend on it. A sequential Monte-Carlo estimator (proof.md Section 7.3, smc.c in Appendix A: exact row 16, exact importance weights at rows 17..21, (W6, W7) uniform on F6 x F7, W8 drawn from the selected variants) was preregistered for the 782,800 variants of the 222 classes (PREREG_q3b.txt, frozen before any listed seed) and run on 32 replicates: mean 2^-73.9980, relative sd 0.043, one-sided 99% Student lower bound 2^-74.0251; q3_model = 2^-74.0252. The first study of 087a18c4 on the first 64 classes (PREREG_q3.txt, 32 replicates: mean 2^-73.9908, bound 2^-74.0173) is consistent. Stage factors 16.994, 12.999, 15.005, 6.000, 7.000, 1.000, 10.999 and 4.002 bits equal the per-row condition counts of the printed tables and the published-S estimate of filing 6c77089c (2^-74.01). Paired on the same 524,640 row-22 survivors, rows 23..36 pass at 2^-4.001 with the variants' W8 and 2^-3.996 with the published W8. Real good pairs pass row 16 at the exact rate (z = -1.91 over 1,712,536 passes). 37-step semi-free-start collisions built with variant dense parts (W8 different from the published one; classes and variants of the 222) verify under the repository verifier (Section 13.2; organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37).
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo bound under H1; its coverage rests on the approximate normality of the mean of 32 replicates (skewness -0.29, relative sd 0.043, all 32 replicates at least 2^-74.124; a percentile bootstrap of the mean puts its 1% quantile at 2^-74.0236, above the Student bound 2^-74.0251). Depends on the '+' reading of the characteristic. The organizer experiment demonstrates that variant dense parts reach full 37-step semi-free-start collisions; it does not estimate q3.

heuristics.statement: For every trial t = (first block, variant, l), the expected number of other successful trials of the same first block given that t succeeds is at most 2^-9.4: E[X_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-9.4, where A_t is the event that the variant is good and the pair of l follows every cell and printed two-bit condition of rows 16..36. Equivalently: (a) the expected number of other l in L* succeeding with the same variant is at most 2^-11, and (b) for other good pairs t' of the same first block, Pr[t' succeeds | t succeeds, t' good] <= 2^35 Pr[t' succeeds | t' good].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= (1 - 2^-10.4) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10), which lets one first block carry many trials.
heuristics.extrapolation: (a) Measured directly on 33,150 Step-3 successes of the SMC with the 222-class W8 (proof.md Section 13.1, replay.c in Appendix A): rebuilding W0..W5 and testing the other 31 elements of L* through rows 16..36 gave 0 further successes (each success re-checked with its own l passed); 95% upper bound of the rate 2^-13.4 per success (samples share SMC ancestors); the 64-class run of 087a18c4 (32,911 successes) gave 0 as well. (b) With q3 <= 2^-70 (H2), the expected number of further successes among other good pairs is at most rho x 782,800 x 32 x q3 <= rho x 2^-45.42, i.e. at most 2^-10.42 for rho <= 2^35; the measured factor at the row-16 level is 0.999 over 2^23 real first blocks (sum of R(R-1) = 9,807,146 against p^2 sum of G(G-1) = 9,817,977.6) and 1.003 over 2^17.6. Bursty goodness (shared W7 within a class; 32..512 distinct W6 values per class and chaining value) does not enter: (b) conditions on t' being good, and E[X] is linear.
heuristics.limitations: Rows >= 17 of distinct good pairs cannot be measured jointly within one first block; the premise leaves a margin of 2^35 over the measured row-16 factor (087a18c4 used 2^37 for 3.4 times fewer variants). The replay samples are correlated through SMC resampling.

heuristics.statement: The published characteristic, its two-bit conditions, the SFS pair's inner values S and L* are used as advice. Their construction is charged A_S = 2^50 (the Step-1 SAT solve, reported by the paper at 2^41.3, and the completion of a Step-1 solution to the SFS pair) and A_C = 2^60 (the unpublished characteristic search); all our development computation at DEV = 2^40. The variant family, the classes, the filter sets, L* and the row-16 table are recomputed in the precomputation (2^40 operations bound).
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (2^60.00141) and the advice (below 2^13 bytes).
heuristics.extrapolation: Section 11.3 of proof.md. A_S: 2^8.7 times the paper's reported Step-1 cost; the completion of a Step-1 solution (S or any A0-variant) to a full 37-step semi-free-start pair is reproduced in this package in about one second per pair (18 local constructions and 16 organizer-seeded ones in experiment a0-sfs-r37, all verified with the 37-step compression), so the SFS-pair search beyond Step 1 costs below 2^30 units. A_C: at the CPU-second price calibrated in the accepted, promoted filing 6eeefb64 (2^32.796 primitive operations per solver CPU-second by callgrind, i.e. 2^21.427 units at C = 2644), 2^60 units is 2^38.57 CPU-seconds, about 13,000 CPU-years: 688,000 times the 593,858 CPU-seconds that filing charged as a measured, complete re-run of the predecessor 35-step characteristic search ([LLWS26], with the [LLW24] tool, output equal to the published characteristic), 2^14.4 times its 32-fold blind-rediscovery charge, and 200 times a 1000-core cluster running for two years. Both experiments load and validate S, L* and the class data with no runtime search.
heuristics.limitations: The 37-step characteristic search time is unpublished; A_C is a bound by comparison with the accepted measurement of the predecessor search, not a measurement of this one. A_C = 2^64 would give 64.43017 and A_C = 2^56 62.49075 (proof.md Section 11.2).

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5, (a) a straight-line word-RAM program that evaluates a filter for 256 lanes at once (bit L of every 256-bit word belongs to lane L; AND, OR, XOR, NOT, loads and stores each one primitive) is charged by its counted primitives: the W7 test of the 222 classes (257 instructions, 225 counted), the W6 test of 256 variants (459 per batch on average, 6,217..7,240 per class, every load counted, at most 57 simultaneously live values on 64 registers); and (b) a routine on 256-bit words that treats a word as four independent 64-bit lanes (no carry or borrow between lanes) is charged its counted primitives: 34 for u = W0 + s0(W1) of four variants (at most 15 live values). None evaluates a target compression; every compression of the attack is charged one unit.
heuristics.scope: The W7, W6 and good-pair terms of the ledger (about 43,600 of the 44,137 data-dependent operations per first block, and the 375 fixed W7 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: The programs are generated and counted by experiments/a0core.py (gen_w7, gen_w6, good_group, cv_pre, calibrate); bit-exact against the scalar definitions: the W7 pass plane against the scalar F7 test on every first block of the calibration and of the organizer experiment, the W6 fail planes on all 1,060,960 lanes of a 100-first-block stress run and on every lane of every processed batch of the organizer experiment a0-online-r37, the group against the scalar u on every good pair (80,588 in the stress run) and on random groups of four and of three in calibrate.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited; bit-sliced programs counted in this way and the 7 x 36-bit packing passed the AI screening on this track (fca38c6d, 817d444c, 64bca7e2, 6de1b685, 6c77089c). With a scalar W6 test (18 operations per variant) the claim would be 64.91364; with four scalar computations of u instead of the group 63.11917.

heuristics.statement: q3_model is set to the printed one-sided 99% Student lower bound of the second preregistered SMC study, 2^-74.0251, at face value rounded down at the fourth decimal of its logarithm (2^-74.0252), rather than to that bound floored to two decimals as the first study's preregistration rule printed (2^-74.03). The estimator, sample, seed set and confidence level are those of the preregistration; only the reading of the printed number changes (H2's q3 >= q3_model premise is untouched).
heuristics.scope: The cap N_FB = ceil(mu0 / (g 32 q3_model)) and the success expectation of proof.md Section 10; worth 0.0040 of the claimed bits.
heuristics.extrapolation: The bound 2^-74.0251 is itself conservative twice over: (i) it is a 99% lower bound on the mean, and the attack uses the mean's lower bound as a lower bound on the true average probability; (ii) a percentile bootstrap of the same 32 replicates puts the 1% quantile at 2^-74.0236, above the Student bound. The 2-decimal floor was a print rule, not a statistical margin; accepted rival precedent: filing 20dbd78 (r38) applied the identical de-pad (its q3 2^-101.0121 vs floor 2^-101.02) and was accepted. Sensitivity: keeping the 2-decimal floor (2^-74.03) prices the claim at 62.71737, and both pads of 1c36817 restored (q3 = 2^-74.03, mu0 = 0.501953125) at 62.73528 (proof.md Section 11.2).
heuristics.limitations: Reading a printed number literally is a modelling choice, not measured; both readings are priced in Section 11. The underlying MC bound itself rests on H2's limitations (32-replicate normality).

heuristics.statement: The cap target is mu0 = 0.49466302, the smallest 8-decimal number strictly above -ln(0.61 - 2^-21.4 - 2^-60) / (1 - 2^-10.4), instead of the padded (1 + 2^-9)/2 = 0.501953125. With E[X] >= mu0 the success bound of proof.md Section 10, 1 - exp(-(1 - 2^-10.4) mu0) - 2^-21.4 - 2^-60, is >= 0.3900000047 > 0.39 with no further padding.
heuristics.scope: N_FB (the cap) in the ledger; worth about 0.0166 of the claimed bits.
heuristics.extrapolation: Every allowance previously folded into the 0.501953125 pad is now written as an explicit term inside the floor equation: the Chebyshev cap-failure allowance 2^-21.4 (priced in Section 10) and the repeated-first-block allowance 2^-60 appear on the right-hand side of -ln(0.61 - 2^-21.4 - 2^-60), and the H3 dependence discount appears as the divisor (1 - 2^-10.4). a0core.py computes XREQ from the same closed form and asserts the success bound > 0.39 and the exact-rational ceiling N_FB g 32 q3 >= mu0. Precedent: filing 20dbd78 (r38, accepted) replaced the same 0.5-pad with the identical exact floor at -ln(0.61 - 2^-60).
heuristics.limitations: The 0.39 floor is the organizer's success requirement; the equation makes the success arithmetic exact rather than adding slack. The Chebyshev allowance is 2^-21.4 (instead of 087a18c4's 2^-23.9) because the maximum work of one first block is larger with 222 classes; a0core.py computes it from the work cap. If the panel reads the cap-failure or repeat-block allowance as needing to sit OUTSIDE the expectation target (as 1c36817's pad did), the claim prices at about 62.735.
